title: Linear-time unary-token encoding
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$ of length $n$, $M$ halts within $c(n+1)$ steps and outputs the pair encoding of the maximal initial run of $1$ bits, including the first following $0$ if there is one, together with the remaining suffix. If the input consists entirely of $1$ bits, the token is the whole input and the remainder is empty.
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the function
splitting its input at the leading unary token --- the maximal leading run
of ones with its terminating zero, if present --- and emitting the
self-delimiting pair encoding of the token and the remainder.
